title: Process
description: A statechart: an entity lifecycle or an orchestration (model/processes/).

use.description: lifecycle: the states an entity goes through. orchestration: a flow of work. library: guards, actions and gates that other processes name by id; it holds nothing that runs (MQ9020).

subjects.description: The entities the process governs, each entry with its own id; an entry covers its entity and the entities derived from it, or names a stereotype and covers every entity that carries it and the entities derived from them. When several entries cover an entity, an entry naming the entity or a base wins, nearest first, then stereotype entries in entry order. A lifecycle lists at least one (MQ9201). Not written together with subject or boundAttribute.

subject.description: The one-subject form, deprecated (MQ9209): use subjects. The entity whose lifecycle this is; required when use is lifecycle and subjects is absent.

boundAttribute.description: The one-subject form, deprecated (MQ9209): use subjects. An enum-typed attribute of the subject that holds the state (lifecycle only).

rightsDefault.description: What the lifecycle answers for a verb when no right of its own holds: allow (also when absent) or deny. Written, even as allow, it makes the project use rights. Lifecycles only (MQ9901).

rationale.description: Markdown text: why the element is shaped this way.

decision.description: A URL or a reference (such as ADR-0042) of the decision record. It is not an element id and is not checked.

excludeStereotypes.description: Stereotype keys that a database schema's or a package's defaultStereotypes would give this element, left out with the stereotypes they imply. Only defaults can be excluded (MQ2029).

gates.description: A library's gates, which a transition names with gatePolicy. A process that is not a library holds its gates on its transitions (MQ9020).

rights.description: The lifecycle's rights, in file order: each allows or denies some actors some verbs, in some states, under an optional condition. An entry is an inline right or a use of a named right (model/rights/). Lifecycles only (MQ9901).

triggerPoints.description: The lifecycle's trigger points, in file order, which is the order they run in at each moment: each says what runs when one of its verbs happens, in some places, under an optional when. A check refuses or warns, an action runs before the checks, with the change or after commit, and a replace takes the place of a built-in effect. Lifecycles only (MQ8101).

states.description: The root's children, in document order. A process that is not a library has at least one, and a library has none (MQ9020).

initial.description: The root's initial child; absent means the first.

not.description: subjects is not written together with the one-subject form (subject, boundAttribute).

subject.title: Subject
subject.description: An entity the process governs, with the entities derived from it; or a stereotype, standing for every entity that carries it and the entities derived from them. Names exactly one of entity and stereotype.

entity.description: The entity. Not written together with stereotype.

stereotype.description: The key of a stereotype that applies to entities (MQ2003, MQ9211): the entry covers every entity that carries it (package defaults, implied stereotypes and its own list, less what it excludes) and every entity derived from one. An entity that an entry naming it or a base also covers follows that entry. Not written together with entity.

boundAttribute.description: The attribute that holds the state (lifecycle only): one of the entity's, own, inherited or from a stereotype it carries; on a stereotype entry, one of the stereotype's own attributes.

owner.description: Where the object's owner is held: a single-valued attribute or a to-one relation end of the entity, own or inherited, or a single-valued attribute of a stereotype the entity or a base carries; on a stereotype entry, a single-valued attribute of the stereotype's own (MQ9606). An actor whose relative is owner reads it. Optional: without it the team's system holds the owner.

right.title: Right
right.description: An entry of a lifecycle's rights: an inline right (name, access, verbs and the rest of what it says) or a use of a named right (right, with states only); exactly one form (MQ9901). An inline right shares its id with its entry.
A use: the id of the named right (kind right) that holds here. Not written with the keys of an inline right (MQ9901).

name.description: An inline right's name, unique among the lifecycle's inline rights (MQ3001); a refusal names it. Required for an inline right (MQ9901).

access.description: An inline right's access: allow or deny. Required for an inline right (MQ9901).

verbs.description: An inline right's verbs, at least one (MQ9901).

states.description: The states of this lifecycle where the right holds (MQ9902); a compound state counts while any state inside it is active, and create is checked in the initial state. Empty: every state.

description.description: Why: shown with every refusal, in the rights grid and in the docs.

triggerPoint.title: Trigger point
triggerPoint.description: An entry of a lifecycle's triggerPoints (part kind process-trigger-point): what runs when one of its verbs happens to the lifecycle's subjects, narrowed by its optional keys. With no narrowing key it runs wherever its verbs happen.

name.description: Unique among the lifecycle's trigger points, and apart from its process's guards (MQ3001); a refusal and a step's assume name it.

states.description: States of this lifecycle the object must be in (for a move, its source); a compound state counts while any state inside it is active, and create is checked in the initial state (MQ8102). Empty: every state.

targets.description: States of this lifecycle a move must enter; a compound state counts when the move enters it or any state inside it, default states included. Beside move verbs, sign, and own verbs an event of this lifecycle names only (MQ8102). Empty: any.

transitions.description: Transitions of this lifecycle a move must be; for sign, a signature on their gates. Beside move verbs, sign, and own verbs an event of this lifecycle names only (MQ8102). Empty: any.

description.description: Why. For a check, the message shown when it refuses or warns; without one, the display name, else the name.

state.title: State
state.description: A state of the process; the root is implicit (the process is the root compound state).

code.description: The state's stable stored value, however the state is stored: a string or an integer. Codes are unique in the process (1 and "1" are one code) and all of one kind; a history or choice state has none (MQ9206).

initial.description: Compound only: the initial child, a direct child (MQ9001); absent means the first child.

defaultTarget.description: History only: the state entered when no history is recorded; absent means the parent's initial.

entry.description: Actions run on entry, in list order.

exit.description: Actions run on exit, in list order.

invoke.description: Invocations started on entry and cancelled on exit, in display order.

states.description: Children in document order; the regions of a parallel state.

transition.title: Transition
transition.description: A transition; among transitions with one source and one trigger, array order is priority.

verb.description: The verb of the automatic move (verbs-design.md decision 12): only on a transition without an event, which takes its event's verb otherwise (MQ9705). A built-in verb's key or one of the project's own (MQ9701).

after.description: An ISO 8601 duration; required when trigger is after.

invoke.description: An invoke of the source; required for invoke-done and invoke-error.

targets.description: None: targetless; several: one per orthogonal region.

actions.description: Actions run on the transition, in list order.

external.description: Whether the source is exited and re-entered when a target is its descendant.

gatePolicy.description: A library's gate, used here instead of an inline gate (MQ9021). Signatures still count per transition.

verb.description: What the actor does by sending the event (verbs-design.md decision 11): a built-in verb's key or one of the project's own (MQ9701). Optional; transitions the event triggers take it.

actors.description: The actors that may send the event; empty means any actor.

guard.title: Guard
guard.description: A named condition; without an expression it is a stub.

expression.description: A JavaScript expression over context and event returning a boolean.

condition.description: The condition as an expression tree over context and event; only true passes. A guard holds expression or condition, not both (MQ3107), or neither as a stub.

action.title: Action
action.description: A named effect: context changes (expression), values set on the object (sets), both, or neither as a stub.

expression.description: A JavaScript expression returning an object of context updates.

sets.description: Values the action sets on the object, each an attribute every subject of the process holds and a value in the expression language. All values are worked out from the object and context as they were when the action started, then applied together. Not in a library (MQ9020).

raises.description: Internal events queued after the action.

set.title: Set
set.description: One attribute of the object set to a value when the action runs.

attribute.description: The attribute set: an attribute every subject of the process holds under one id (an id, or the keyed id of an inherited or contributed attribute). Not derived, and not one that holds a lifecycle's state (MQ9801, MQ9802); once per action (MQ9803).

value.description: The value, which reads what a guard reads (the context, the object under subject, the payload of the events whose transitions list the action, now(), current_actor(), in_state) and fits the attribute's type (MQ3103). Null clears the attribute.

invoke.title: Invoke
invoke.description: Work a state starts on entry: a sub-process, a service task or a human task.

actors.description: Who may complete a human task.

gate.title: Gate
gate.description: A signature gate on an event transition: the transition fires on the occurrence that completes the gate.

signers.description: The actors whose members may sign.

requiredActors.description: Actors each of which must give at least one signature (a subset of signers).

allowRepeatSigner.description: Whether one signer may count twice.

reasonRequired.description: Whether each signature must carry a reason.

auditAttributes.description: Extra fields recorded with each signature.
